claims.statement: The HO-4 2013-07 edition is superseded by HO-4 2021-10 for policies effective on or after 2021-10-01, while 2013-07 remains applicable to policies written under that edition; the two forms have effective dates 2013-07-01 and 2021-10-01 respectively.

Both HO-4 editions expressly provide no Coverage A, so the policy does not insure the dwelling or building property under Coverage A; Coverage D and some additional-coverages provisions nevertheless reference a Coverage A limit and must not be converted into assumed dwelling coverage.

HO-4 organizes property protection through Coverage B Other Structures, Coverage C Personal Property, and Coverage D Loss of Use, while Section I Coverage E contains Additional Coverages and Section II Coverage E and Coverage F provide Personal Liability and Medical Payments to Others.

Coverage B's core repair settlement is not the previously asserted edition difference: 2013-07 B.20 settles a covered loss under the applicable valuation provision, caps payment at the amount necessary to repair or replace, and excludes betterment, matching, and non-restorative improvements; 2021-10 B.19 covers repair or replacement of the damaged portion with like kind and quality and excludes an ordinance-or-law cost increase unless the policy otherwise provides it.

The 2021-10 Coverage C special limits increased from 2013-07 for electronic apparatus in a motor vehicle, money and precious metals, theft of jewelry/watches/precious stones, theft of firearms, watercraft, and business property on the residence premises; the silverware limit remained $2,500 in both editions.

Coverage D's stated limit differs by edition: 2013-07 expressly sets it at 30% of Coverage A; 2021-10 states a forty-percent Coverage D limit, and the filing memorandum identifies that revised relationship as 40% of Coverage A. Both editions provide additional living expense, fair rental value, and civil-authority loss-of-use coverage subject to their own conditions and limits.

The HO-4 base forms exclude major water boundaries including flood or surface water, subsurface water, sewer or drain backup, sump overflow or discharge, and continuous or repeated seepage or leakage, along with deterioration and fungi, wet rot, dry rot, or bacteria conditions; covered accidental discharge is subject to the applicable edition's peril wording and exclusions.

Both editions impose material post-loss duties including notice, protection and retention of damaged property, records and inventory, examination under oath, sworn proof of loss within 60 days after request, cooperation, disclosure of other insurance, and preservation of recovery rights; appraisal determines amount of loss rather than coverage. The 2013-07 form makes payment due within 60 days after agreement, a binding appraisal award, or final judgment, while 2021-10 states payment within 60 days after agreement on the amount of loss, subject to applicable conditions.

Section II Coverage E pays covered occurrence-based bodily-injury or property-damage liability and provides a defense for a covered suit until the applicable liability limit is exhausted; Coverage F pays qualifying medical expenses to persons other than insureds without regard to fault, generally for expenses incurred within three years of the accident, subject to edition-specific exclusions.

HO 04 92 Water Backup — Tenants (2019-03), when attached, writes back limited direct-physical-loss coverage for covered personal property caused by defined water backup, subject to a $2,500 limit and $250 deductible; it preserves the other policy's exclusions and conditions and does not create coverage for otherwise ineligible property.

HO 04 27 Limited Water Damage Coverage (2016-05), when attached, modifies HO-4 water-damage terms by covering specified sudden and accidental discharge, overflow, breakage, or freezing events and preserves exclusions for repeated seepage, sewer/drain/sump backup, subsurface water, flood, fungi/rot/bacteria, and failed diversion systems; its stated limits include $2,500 for backup/sump overflow and $5,000 for fungi, wet or dry rot, or bacteria.

The seeded HO 04 61 Scheduled Personal Property editions and HO 04 65 Coverage C Increased Special Limits edition identify their line as HO-3 rather than HO-4, so they should not be applied as HO-4 endorsements without an applicable attachment or schedule establishing that use.

The 2021-10 filing memorandum is an interpretive filing map describing revisions to deductible administration, policy continuation, mold wording, claim-handling authority, Coverage D and special-limit presentation, post-loss conditions, and Section II liability wording; it does not itself grant coverage, so the governing form, declarations, and attached endorsements control if wording differs.

The editions present the named-peril grant differently: 2013-07 uses a separate Perils Insured Against section requiring direct physical loss caused by a listed named peril, while 2021-10 uses its Section I peril provisions to state direct-physical-loss grants, water-system qualifications, resulting-loss treatment, and location and causation boundaries; the applicable edition's exact peril clause controls.

Personal-property settlement must be read from the governing edition's valuation provisions: 2013-07 defines actual cash value and replacement cost and expressly permits adjustment by actual cash value, repair, replacement, or provision for repair or replacement; 2021-10 separately defines actual cash value and replacement cost and gives general conditions for inspection of repaired property, repair estimates, salvage, and taking damaged property at agreed or appraised value, without the previously asserted pairs-and-sets, unavailable-parts, or Coverage C-specific lesser-of formula in the cited form text.

The Section II additional property-damage coverage increased from a $1,000 maximum in 2013-07 to a $1,500 maximum in 2021-10; 2013-07 requires the damaged property to be in the care of a person other than an insured, while 2021-10 makes payment available regardless of legal liability and retains edition-specific property relationship exclusions and exceptions.

For a tenant, Section II liability does not insure the tenant's own contents as liability property damage or automatically cover the landlord's dwelling: the editions exclude property owned by, rented to, occupied by, used by, or in the care of an insured, with 2021-10 expressly preserving stated fire, smoke, or explosion exceptions for certain rented, occupied, or loaned property.

Both base HO-4 editions can cover sudden accidental water discharge or overflow damage to qualifying personal property while excluding the dwelling, building systems, and the source-system property under their base wording; water backup, flood or surface water, subsurface water, gradual seepage, and fungi or rot remain subject to the edition-specific exclusions and any attached endorsement.

The supplied Texas HO 01 45 2022-01 state amendatory form is an HO-3 form, not an HO-4 form; state-form terms should be applied only within the scope of the issued and attached state form rather than transplanted into the Mississippi HO-4 comparison.
